Vancini Conversions Turns a Regular Sprinter Into a Custom, Fully-Equipped Mobile Podcast Studio
26 photos
Photo: Vancini Conversions
Turning a cargo van into a mobile living space is just one of the many ways in which you can give an ordinary vehicle a new purpose. These versatile vehicles can be transformed into almost anything you want, from mobile businesses and healthcare clinics to traveling workshops and more.
Luckily, there are many van outfitters out there that are not afraid to think outside the box when it comes to creating unique conversions. One of them is Vancini Conversions, whose latest creation is a beautiful mobile podcast and event studio.
Panel and cargo vans offer a great combination of mobility, practicality, and adaptability that makes them suitable for a wide range of uses, including businesses and creative pursuits that don’t necessarily need a permanent physical location to operate. A podcast studio is something that can be set up inside a van, giving more freedom of movement and allowing you to take conversations, stories, and community voices on the road.
For those who don’t know, Vancini Conversions is a Canadian custom van conversion shop that builds one-of-a-kind van conversions for both adventure and commercial applications. The Ontario-based team has considerable experience in woodworking and van conversions, and they only work on commission, so each build is specifically tailored to the customer’s needs and aspirations. In this case, they used their extensive know-how to turn a regular cargo van into an awesome mobile podcast studio.
Photo: Vancini Conversions Built for SEIU Healthcare, a local union representing healthcare workers, this conversion is of the most unique builds to leave the Vancini shop and a great example of what’s possible when a project is specifically designed around its intended purpose.
It’s based on a 2026 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 170-EXT and comes with a nice setup for producing content on the road, two workstations, professional recording equipment, and a robust electrical system.
The van’s exterior looks phenomenal with its custom purple wrap by Branded Wraps, and it would be hard to miss it on the road. But otherwise, the outside is very minimal. The company only installed a couple of small windows, a Flatline Van Company roof rack, a Fiamma F45S awning, and Atlas Roadcamp side steps.
All the magic happens inside, where the team at Vancini created a welcoming creative workspace. Modern materials and finishes, such as Corian countertops, laminate Baltic birch cabinetry in sleek black, Lonseal flooring, and upholstered gray walls, give it a contemporary appearance. The clear cedar on the ceiling adds a warm touch, while purple accents ties the exterior design language with the interior.
Photo: Vancini Conversions The front section is occupied by an L-shaped sofa with upholstery from Shady Lady Hamilton. Finished in purple, it provides comfortable seating for podcast guests and creates a welcoming setting for conversations and interviews. It comes accompanied by a custom-made adjustable table, while two large 55-inch LG 4K OLED TVs occupy the surrounding wall space.
These massive screens can serve as dynamic backdrops during recordings. A side table next to the sofa integrates a small Vitrifrigo fridge for refreshments and a drawer for storage.
On the ceiling, the builder installed a heavy-duty L-track system, allowing for up to three cameras to be mounted up there and positioned as needed to capture video from multiple angles.
The central area of the van is dedicated to a generous workstation with a full-width table and two chairs. Three 32-inch Dell 4K monitors are positioned around this area, with two installed on swivel mounts the side walls and another on a custom mount. One section of the table folds down to create a passageway toward the rear of the van, and an L-track for securing the chairs when on the move are also included.
Photo: Vancini Conversions Smart storage solutions are also incorporated. For instance, all the space under the front sofa is storage, and one section of the central table is only attached magnetically and can be removed to access a secret storage compartment. THis provides a perfect place for cameras, lenses, and stuff like that. A floor-to-ceiling cabinet at the back of the van adds even more vertical storage for gear and other items, while Van Essential rear-door storage bags make it easy to keep brochures, flyers, and other materials organized.
The van was designed with different lighting zones to allow owners to set the mood, and multiple wall-mounted plugs with adapters for HDMI and USB-C will allow them to charge their devices.
Behind all this, a robust electrical system keeps everything running smoothly. It includes 920Ah of heated Blizzard lithium batteries, a Victron MultiPlus-II 12/3000 inverter/charger, an Orion 50A DC-DC charger and a Victron 100/30 solar charge controller. A 400-watt solar array on the roof allows for off-grid operations. The brain of the van is a Cerbo GX MK2 with a Victron Touch 70, which provides centralized monitoring and control.
Photo: Vancini Conversions This mobile podcast studio can be used in any season thanks to a Nomadic Cooling 12V X3 Helix air-conditioner, a Maxxair 7500K roof fan for ventilation, and a 4kW Eberspächer diesel heater. There is no plumbing system inside this van.
With its stylish design, extensive equipment, and reliable power system this Vancini van conversion is expected to handle recording sessions, broadcasting, and remote performance setups successfully.
